Mule
mūl
n. (a hybrid beast of burden; rendering Hebrew pered)
From Latin mulus. Mules were not bred in Israel, since the law forbade mixing kinds — they were imported, and they were royal.

Biblical Definition

A mule is a hybrid beast. David's mule carries Solomon to his anointing at Gihon: “cause Solomon my son to ride upon mine own mule” (1Ki 1:33) — the king's own mount being the visible sign of succession. Absalom dies when his mule goes out from under him and his head is caught in an oak (2Sa 18:9). The psalmist warns, “Be ye not as the horse, or as the mule, which have no understanding” (Psa 32:9).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines mule as a quadruped of a mongrel breed, usually generated between an ass and a mare, sometimes between a horse and a she-ass.

expand to see more

MULE, n. A quadruped of a mongrel breed, usually generated between an ass and a mare, sometimes between a horse and a she-ass.

2. A plant formed by impregnating the pistil of one species with the farin or fecundating dust of another.

Key Scripture

1Ki 1:33 — "The king also said unto them, Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride upon mine own mule, and bring him down to Gihon:"

2Sa 18:9 — "And Absalom met the servants of David. And Absalom rode upon a mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that was under him went away."

Psa 32:9 — "Be ye not as the horse, or as the mule, which have no understanding: whose mouth must be held in with bit and bridle, lest they come near unto thee."

Psa 32:8 — "I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way which thou shalt go: I will guide thee with mine eye."

Modern Corruption

Guidance is asked for and then resisted, and Psalm 32 pictures the difference between being led by an eye and being hauled by a bit.

expand to see more

Psalm 32:8-9 sets two methods side by side. I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way which thou shalt go: I will guide thee with mine eye. Then the warning: be ye not as the horse, or as the mule, which have no understanding: whose mouth must be held in with bit and bridle. Guidance by eye requires the guided party to be watching; guidance by bit works on an animal that is not. God offers the first and is willing to use the second, and which one a believer receives depends largely on where he is looking.

Absalom's death carries a bitter irony worth noting. The mule went away from under him — the beast simply kept walking — and the man renowned for his hair was left hanging by his head. Nothing struck him down; his mount continued and he did not.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew pered (H6505), a mule; pirdah (H6506), a she-mule — David's own mount in 1 Kings 1.

expand to see more

Hebrew pered (H6505) — mule; 2 Samuel 18:9, Psalm 32:9, 1 Kings 10:25.

Hebrew pirdah (H6506) — she-mule; 1 Kings 1:33, 38, 44, ride upon mine own mule.

Usage

"“Cause Solomon my son to ride upon mine own mule” — succession made visible."

"“Be ye not as the horse, or as the mule” — led by eye or hauled by bit."

"“The mule that was under him went away” — Absalom left hanging."
